newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SOCCER-BOCA WIN 6-0 AFTER A WEEK OF CRISIS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BOCA WIN 6-0 AFTER A WEEK OF CRISIS.

text.p: Boca Juniors, Argentina's most popular team, recovered from a week of internal strife and upheaval to thrash Huracan 6-0 at the weekend.

Failure to beat Huracan would almost certainly have led to the sack for Carlos Bilardo, who has taken most of the blame for the poor performance of a team which cost an estimated $15 million to assemble -- a huge amount by local standards.

Boca, who had been expected to win the championship, had dropped to tenth place last week after losing 3-1 to lowly Banfield -- even though the squad had been offered $1 million in prize money if they won all their remaining matches.
There was further trouble during the week when Bilardo dropped goalkeeper Carlos Navarro Montoya, who responded by saying: "The substitutes' bench is no place for me."
But Boca, helped by the first half sending off of Huracan striker Claudio Garcia, appeared to forget their problems after Julio Toresani put them ahead in the 16th minute.
A penalty by Sebastian Rambert and a header by Nestor Fabbri gave Boca a 3-0 halftime lead. Uruguay's Gabriel Cedres, Diego Latorre and Riquelme scored in the second half.

When he took over just under a year ago, Bilardo had promised that visting teams at the Bombonera stadium would not get out of their own half but this was the first time his promise had come close to being fulfilled.
Unfashionable Lanus, who come from a Buenos Aires suburb, went top of the table by beating Newell's Old Boys 2-0 with goals in each half by Ariel Lopez and Ariel Ibagaza.
They overtook River Plate, who are in Tokyo for Tuesday's Intercontintal Cup match against Juventus of Italy.
